anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing, runtime state collection, packet field collection and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable packet_sig value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

primary_anchor.source_export: closure returned by exported u(config); the runtime config binds slot 23
primary_anchor.answer_basis: Agent-visible corpus only: the canonical anchor answer is captured_span plus answer_function as declared in the captured bundle slice. source_function is a private maintainer mapping into src/.
primary_anchor.naming_note: source_function (z, the closure inside the exported reducer factory u) is renamed to t in the obfuscated bundle; graders must match captured_span (hash/offset) and answer_function, not the source-side identifier.
primary_anchor.why: First target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic chain. Its own body selects the runtime reducer variant via q(), runs the selected reducer to compute the hash fold, then formats and returns the final ss_-prefixed packet_sig string. All upstream functions only route, collect, or schedule inputs; the factory u only returns this closure.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span in the captured bundle (hash/offset/complete function body). Agents only see captures, so the standard answer identifier is primary_anchor.answer_function (t), not source_function (z).

A returned function name is scored against answer_function in the captured corpus. source_function is a private maintainer label and is not something an agent can know unless the bundle still exposes that exact identifier.
Agent explanation distinguishes the anchor from routing, input preparation, the reducer factory wrapper, the console sink, core utilities and off-chain decoy functions.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function in the captured corpus.
Identifying u as the anchor is accepted only if the agent clearly attributes the value construction to the closure it returns (answer_function t) rather than to u's own body.

role_oracle.why: Selects the runtime reducer variant with q(), runs reducers[pick] to compute the packet-specific hash fold, and formats the result into the final ss_-prefixed packet_sig string.

The main reducer body invoked by the anchor. Combines tuple scoring, text construction, accumulator initialization, per-character mixing, and finalization to produce the hash fold and length passed to the formatter.
Selects which of the 8 reducer variants to use based on branch, mask, route score, tuple score, runtime ticket, and slot. Only reachable through the anchor; target-specific.
Formats the reducer output into the final ss_<body>_<tail> string using the slot-derived width. Strictly below the anchor; not a generic utility since it encodes the target-specific ss_ prefix logic.
Builds the ordered text string hashed by the reducer. Applies variant-dependent ordering and row joining. Only reachable through o().
Initializes the hash accumulator using the basis constant, config mask/slot, variant, tuple score, and salt string. Only reachable through o().
Mixes each character into the accumulator using a variant-selected prime and rotate; only reachable through o().
Finalizes the hash fold by mixing in route array entries and applying avalanche steps. Only reachable through o().
Orders packet field parts according to the variant-specific index list, filling missing entries with a default. Only reachable through k() and o().
Serializes a single packet field part into a colon-delimited row string using one of four variant-specific field orderings. Only reachable through k() and o().
Generic 32-bit left-rotate utility used by the per-character mixer.
Generic unsigned base36 fixed-width formatter used by s$1 to encode the hash fold integer.
Generates the static 'ss_' prefix via a character-code array map. Used by s$1; it has no inputs and produces a fixed string.
Factory that binds the runtime config and returns the anchor closure t. Its own body does not compute any hash or format any value; it only creates and returns the anchor function.
Assembles the final payload and emits it via a dynamic console method. Receives an already-generated reducedValue; does not construct the packet_sig itself.

empty_roles.why_empty: Path-critical upstream functions (delegated click listener, command hub, state machine driver, middleware, async scheduler, contract resolver) exist in the bundle but their exact captured spans are not enumerated in this role_oracle entry set. They would score 0.2 if identified correctly.
Generic path helpers (DOM readers, normalizers, query canonicalizers) exist in the upstream chain but are not enumerated here. They would score 0.1.

Off-chain decoys (the x00-x43 alternate-slot reducers, the v00-v24 vendor noise modules, and the console.debug/info shadow emitters) are not enumerated as individual spans. They are handled by scoring_policy.decoy_answer and score 0 regardless of structural similarity to the anchor.

scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span; the anchor t is nested inside the factory u, so a submission matching t scores 1 (Anchor) and one matching u scores 0.2 (Path/Wrapper)
scoring_policy.answer_identifier: Grade primarily by captured_span (hash/offset/complete function body); the secondary check is submission.function_name === role_oracle[].answer_function. source_function does not participate in default agent scoring.
scoring_policy.decoy_answer: score_zero — x00-x43 files are off-chain decoys regardless of structural similarity to anchor

do_not_promote: The reducer factory u (answer_function u) creates the anchor but does not itself construct the packet_sig value.
Upstream routing, click delegation, command dispatch, and state machine functions only move control and data to the anchor.
The console sink r$g emits an already-computed value; it does not implement the hash logic.
The 8 reducer variants all produce ss_ values, but only the variant selected by slot 23 at runtime feeds the target packet_sig field.
x00-x43 decoy files implement structurally similar ss_ generators for other slot indices; they are off-chain and score zero.
Shadow console.debug and console.info outputs (from the q0 j function) carry packet.shadow values but do not feed the target console.log field.
Identifying any single helper from t9.js (o, q, s$1, k, l, m$1, n$1, h$1, j$1) without the anchor closure t earns 0.7 at best.
debug_hints_private: The anchor closure in the captured bundle is function t(w, y = {}) at line 85, offset 3252.
The reducer factory export u corresponds to bundle function u at line 84; its returned closure (source name z) is bundle function t.
The config has slot 23 (0x17); this is encoded in the runtime configuration that binds to the closure.
Source paths are private evaluator mapping aids, not the default answer space for agents.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Returned span maps uniquely to the anchor closure (answer_function t, bundle lines 85-88, offset 3252-3363).
Returned span maps to one of the nested target-specific helpers: o, q, s$1, k, l, m$1, n$1, h$1, or j$1.
Returned span maps to a generic utility directly used by the anchor: r$h (left-rotate), b$j (base36), or p$2 (ss_ prefix).
Returned span maps to u (factory/wrapper), the sink r$g, or an upstream path-critical routing or scheduling function.
Returned span maps to an x00-x43 decoy, a v00-v24 vendor noise function, or cannot be uniquely mapped to a captured function.
